questions.question_text: Which of the following is a key requirement for a valid test session?
options: Having a friend present to help with the computer
Ensuring your face is clearly visible and your ears are not covered
Using a physical dictionary during the writing section
Writing the test on a mobile phone while commuting
questions.explanation: Test security protocols require that your face and ears remain visible to the proctoring software throughout the exam.

questions.question_text: When writing an essay for the exam, why is it important to use a variety of sentence structures?
options: To meet the minimum word count
To demonstrate a high level of language proficiency
To make the essay easier for the computer to grade
To confuse the reader
questions.explanation: Using a mix of simple, compound, and complex sentences shows the evaluator that you have advanced control over English grammar.

questions.question_text: What is the consequence of writing 'off-topic' in your essay response?
options: You will get extra points for creativity
Your score for the writing task will be significantly lowered
The system will automatically restart the section
It has no effect on the score
questions.explanation: Essays are graded based on relevance to the prompt; failing to address the topic directly negatively impacts the score.

questions.question_text: How should you approach a prompt that asks you to describe an image?
options: List every single object you see
Write a creative story that has nothing to do with the image
Describe the scene, the people, and the actions clearly
Only write one short sentence
questions.explanation: A strong description provides a cohesive overview of the image, including the 'who', 'what', and 'where' shown in the picture.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is best practice when reviewing your writing?
options: Check for spelling and punctuation errors
Change all your words to more complex synonyms
Remove all adjectives to save time
Delete the introduction if you run out of time
questions.explanation: Proofreading is essential to catch simple mistakes that could lower your score despite your vocabulary knowledge.

questions.question_text: If you are asked to write about a personal experience, what should you focus on?
options: Abstract theories
Clear, logical storytelling with descriptive details
Using as many technical terms as possible
Writing in a highly formal, academic style only
questions.explanation: Personal narratives should be engaging and organized, showing the examiner you can articulate a sequence of events.

questions.question_text: What is a key requirement for a valid test session?
options: A fast internet connection and a working webcam.
A second monitor to display the questions.
Having a friend present to verify your work.
Writing your answers on paper first.
questions.explanation: The test requires a stable connection and a camera to ensure security throughout the exam.

questions.question_text: Why is using varied sentence structures important in your essay?
options: It makes the essay shorter.
It demonstrates a higher level of language proficiency.
It is required to fill up the word count.
It ensures the spelling checker works correctly.
questions.explanation: Varying structure shows you can handle complex grammatical rules and nuance.

questions.question_text: What happens if your essay response is off-topic?
options: The system automatically gives you a passing score.
The score will be negatively impacted because you failed the prompt.
You are given a second chance to rewrite it.
The word count is ignored.
questions.explanation: Prompt adherence is a critical part of the assessment criteria for writing.

questions.question_text: How should you approach a prompt asking you to describe an image?
options: Focus only on the background.
Provide a detailed description of objects, actions, and settings.
Ignore the image and write about your favorite hobby.
Ask a question to the proctor about the image.
questions.explanation: Image description tasks test your ability to use descriptive language and vocabulary.

questions.question_text: What is best practice when reviewing your writing?
options: Change all your words to more complex ones at the last second.
Check for spelling, grammar, and clarity.
Delete half the essay to make it more concise.
Translate it into another language to check it.
questions.explanation: Proofreading ensures that you haven't made careless mistakes that could lower your score.

questions.question_text: If asked to write about a personal experience, what should you focus on?
options: Using as many technical terms as possible.
Sharing your feelings and specific details about the event.
Writing as many words as you can in the time limit.
Avoiding the use of 'I' or 'me'.
questions.explanation: Personal experience essays are scored based on the ability to narrate and reflect naturally.

questions.question_text: Why should you use varied sentence structures in your essays?
options: It makes the essay shorter.
It demonstrates advanced writing proficiency and keeps the reader engaged.
It is required by the computer to count the words faster.
It helps you avoid using punctuation.
questions.explanation: Varied sentence length and complexity are key indicators of high-level language fluency in writing assessments.

questions.question_text: What is the consequence of writing 'off-topic' in your response?
options: You receive extra points for creativity.
The score will be negatively impacted because you failed to answer the prompt.
The test will automatically restart.
It is ignored as long as the spelling is correct.
questions.explanation: Answering the specific prompt is essential; writing about an unrelated topic proves a lack of comprehension.

questions.question_text: How should you approach a prompt to describe an image?
options: List every single pixel you see.
Write a coherent paragraph covering the main subjects and the context of the scene.
Copy a generic description from a book.
Only describe the colors used in the image.
questions.explanation: A good description provides context and detailed observations rather than a simple, disjointed list.

questions.question_text: What is best practice when reviewing your written response?
options: Check for spelling, grammar, and ensure you answered the entire prompt.
Change all your sentences to be very short.
Delete your work and start over if you have time.
Add as many filler words as possible.
questions.explanation: Reviewing allows you to correct minor errors and ensure the content fully addresses the task requirements.

questions.question_text: Which element is crucial for a valid test session?
options: Writing your essay in a public area.
Ensuring your face remains visible to the camera at all times.
Using a thesaurus to find obscure words.
Writing for as long as the timer allows, even if finished.
questions.explanation: Security protocols require you to stay in the view of the camera to prevent cheating.

questions.question_text: How do you ensure your writing remains cohesive?
options: By repeating the prompt at the end of each paragraph.
By using transition words to connect your ideas logically.
By using only one sentence per paragraph.
By avoiding all pronouns.
questions.explanation: Cohesion is built by logically linking sentences and ideas using transition words like 'however,' 'furthermore,' and 'therefore.'

questions.question_text: What should be your primary goal in a 5-minute writing task?
options: Producing as many pages as possible.
Writing a clear, well-structured response that directly answers the prompt.
Including as many complex idioms as possible.
Using only passive voice.
questions.explanation: Quality and clarity are prioritized over length, provided the prompt is answered thoroughly.
